newsitem.title: USA: CS First Boston faces SEC action over Orange County.
newsitem.headline: CS First Boston faces SEC action over Orange County.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission has told CS First Boston Corp. that it plans to bring fraud charges against the firm in connections with Orange County, Calif., bonds, it was disclosed Monday.

The commission has authorised the filing of a civil enforcement action against CS First Boston, alleging violations of the anti-fraud statutes of the federal securities laws, according to Orange County documents obtained by Reuters.
The SEC has been investigating CS First Boston's due diligence as underwriter of county taxable pension obligation bonds. CS First Boston is a unit of CS Holding.
According to the documents, CS First Boston told the county that the firm "believes it has meritorious defences to any such SEC action and intends to defend it vigorously."
SEC associate regional director of enforcement in Los Angeles Sandra Harris declined to comment. A spokesman for CS First Boston was not immediately available for comment.
The disclosures were included in county documents prepared as part of its proposed refunding of county pension bonds.
Orange County filed for bankruptcy protection on Dec. 6, 1994, after sustaining investment losses of more than $1.6 billion. It emerged from bankruptcy in June of this year.
Soon after the county declared bankruptcy, the SEC initiated a sweeping investigation of its massive borrowings.

The SEC has already filed complaints against the county's former treasurer and assistant treasurer, alleging they made misleading statements in the offer and sale of more than $2.1 billion of municipal securities.
SEC staff has also been investigating several local governments in connection with the bankruptcy as well as several bond professionals, including Merrill Lynch & Co.
